ai.definition: Chronological Communication refers to the theoretical transfer of information across temporal boundaries, leveraging either tachyonic particles or wormhole bridges.
ai.howItWorks: This technology theoretically uses closed timelike curves (CTCs) to send signals back to a previous state of the universe. CTCs are hypothetical paths in spacetime that allow for travel into the past under certain conditions, which could enable data transfer through time.
ai.problemSolved: It addresses the challenge of transmitting information across temporal gaps, potentially allowing for real-time communication with historical events or future scenarios.
ai.manufacturing: Currently theoretical and not manufacturable due to its reliance on unproven concepts such as CTCs and tachyons. Manufacturing processes are non-existent at this stage.
ai.buildProcess: A build process is not applicable in the current state of theory, but would involve advanced physics and engineering principles if realized.
ai.costDrivers: Current cost drivers include theoretical research, computational modeling, and potential future materials development for tachyons or wormholes. Costs are speculative at this stage.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Theoretical and speculative; requires significant scientific breakthroughs to become practical.
ai.regulation: Non-existent due to the purely theoretical nature of the technology. Any future regulatory framework would depend on the realization of the underlying physics.
ai.risks: High risk due to reliance on unproven physical theories, potential ethical implications if realized, and challenges in verification and validation.
ai.profitability: Not applicable at this stage as the technology is purely theoretical and not commercially viable. Potential future profitability would depend on successful realization of the underlying physics and technological advancements.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development could involve significant progress in quantum mechanics, relativity theory, and materials science to support tachyonic or wormhole-based communication systems.

glossary.def: Hypothetical paths in spacetime that allow for travel into the past under certain conditions.
Theoretical particles that always move faster than light and can potentially be used to transmit information across time.
Hypothetical tunnels through spacetime that could provide shortcuts for travel between distant points in space or even across time, depending on the nature of CTCs.

subsystems.name: Spacetime channel
subsystems.role: the geometry through which the signal travels — a traversable wormhole throat, or a faster-than-light particle path.
parts: geometry shaped so a closed timelike curve connects two events

subsystems.name: Exotic-energy source
subsystems.role: holds the channel open; ordinary matter makes a wormhole pinch shut.
parts: Casimir-type vacuum engineering (the only lab-observed negative energy effect)

subsystems.name: Transmitter
subsystems.role: encodes information onto whatever the channel carries.
parts: encoding scheme able to survive the transit

subsystems.name: Receiver
subsystems.role: detects and decodes the signal at the arrival event.

subsystems.name: Consistency layer
subsystems.role: keeps the message from creating a paradox, e.g. a message that prevents its own sending.
parts: verification of received content against the causal record

buildSteps.title: Choose a candidate geometry
buildSteps.detail: Start from a known solution of Einstein's field equations that contains closed timelike curves — for example a rotating universe, a rotating cylinder, or a traversable wormhole whose mouths are given a relative motion.

buildSteps.title: Work out the energy requirement
buildSteps.detail: Calculate the stress-energy tensor the geometry needs, and check whether it demands negative energy density and how much.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the exotic energy
buildSteps.detail: This is the hard step. The only measured source of negative energy density is the Casimir effect between closely spaced plates, and quantum inequalities appear to bound it far too tightly for any macroscopic bridge.

buildSteps.title: Open and stabilise the throat
buildSteps.detail: Assemble enough negative energy at the throat to counter the gravitational pinch, and suppress any instability that would collapse it.

buildSteps.title: Create the time offset
buildSteps.detail: Give the two ends of the channel a relative velocity or place one in a strong gravitational field, so clocks at the two ends drift apart and the link crosses into its own past.

buildSteps.title: Establish the signal path
buildSteps.detail: Launch a carrier — a laser or microwave beam, a particle stream, or (if they exist) tachyons — through the channel and confirm it emerges at the far end.

buildSteps.title: Encode and transmit
buildSteps.detail: Modulate the carrier with data and send it. The encoding must be robust to the extreme redshift, noise and possibly unknown physics of the transit.

buildSteps.title: Receive and check consistency
buildSteps.detail: Decode the message and test whether it implies a self-contradictory history. If it does, the transmission must have been impossible, which is itself the experiment's most informative result.

prerequisites.why: mathematically valid spacetimes containing time loops have been known since the late 1940s; the theory is not the obstacle.
published solutions exist for wormholes a person could in principle pass through — on paper, not in nature.

prerequisites.tech: Negative energy density at macroscopic scale
prerequisites.why: holding a wormhole open needs a quantity of negative energy that known quantum effects cannot remotely supply.
there are strong arguments that quantum effects destroy any time machine at the moment it forms; until that is settled, no design can be trusted.
tachyons are hypothetical, have never been observed, and would generally allow causality-violating signals, which is exactly why most physicists doubt they exist.

pathway.milestone: mathematical study of time-loop spacetimes and self-consistency rules
pathway.unlocks: a precise statement of what would have to be true for such a channel to exist.

pathway.milestone: tabletop analogue experiments that simulate closed timelike curves in optics or cold atoms
pathway.unlocks: tests of the logic of self-consistency — but only for the analogue system, not real spacetime.

pathway.milestone: precision tests of quantum inequalities and the chronology protection argument
pathway.unlocks: a firm yes-or-no on whether any macroscopic time bridge could ever be stable.

pathway.milestone: laboratory control of vacuum energy on macroscopic scales
pathway.unlocks: if achievable at all, the exotic-matter technology that every design for this depends on — with consequences far beyond communication.
